thesis: Research taste is a set of revisable probabilistic world-model priors about research dynamics: which problem transformations, observations, experiments, and stopping decisions are likely to produce the most useful reduction in uncertainty and future capability under current budget, authority, and world constraints.

candidatePriors.name: burden_before_abstraction
candidatePriors.claim: A recurring observed burden or failure is a better predictor of useful structure than conceptual appeal or taxonomy completeness.
candidatePriors.failureBoundary: Novel domains can require anticipatory infrastructure before repeated burden appears; use credible non-bypassable responsibility evidence rather than demanding repeated production failure in every case.

candidatePriors.name: discriminating_falsifier_before_solution
candidatePriors.claim: When several explanations or architectures remain plausible, the smallest experiment that can separate them usually creates more useful progress per unit cost than implementing the broad solution first.
candidatePriors.failureBoundary: If no bounded observation can discriminate the alternatives, a larger instrumentation or environment investment may itself be the smallest useful experiment.

candidatePriors.name: closed_loop_cost_determines_tractability
candidatePriors.claim: Generation or implementation cost alone is a poor measure of tractability; verification latency, observation quality, recovery work, effect ambiguity, and repeated human intervention can dominate the improvement loop.
candidatePriors.failureBoundary: For pure deterministic local computation with cheap exact verification, generation/compute cost may dominate and the larger closed-loop model adds little.

candidatePriors.name: strong_simpler_baseline_before_new_structure
candidatePriors.claim: A new Agent-native structure should beat a mature classical or materially simpler Agent baseline before its complexity is treated as leverage.
candidatePriors.failureBoundary: A baseline can be cheap but incapable of expressing the target property; comparison must preserve the actual semantic objective rather than reward an easier task.

candidatePriors.name: reversibility_expands_searchable_space
candidatePriors.claim: Private, reversible, recoverable experiments make a larger portion of the hypothesis space practically searchable because failed interventions have lower consequence and retry cost.
candidatePriors.failureBoundary: Some phenomena only exist under real irreversible or social consequence; simulation and reversible proxies can then misrepresent the dynamics.

candidatePriors.name: observability_precedes_optimization
candidatePriors.claim: A problem is poorly tractable when the relevant state, transition, or consequence cannot be observed with enough fidelity to distinguish improvement from noise or false completion.
candidatePriors.failureBoundary: Instrumentation itself has cost and can perturb the world; perfect observability is neither required nor generally available.

candidatePriors.name: materially_different_recurrence_before_generalization
candidatePriors.claim: A semantic relation may be shared after one domain, but a shared mechanism or new layer usually requires recurrence across materially different consumers or worlds.
candidatePriors.failureBoundary: A responsibility can be non-bypassable and universal by construction even before multiple consumers exist; the burden of proof then comes from the underlying substrate contract rather than recurrence count.

candidatePriors.name: contraction_is_a_discovery_operator
candidatePriors.claim: Deletion, narrowing, localization, and archive tests often reveal the actual invariant more efficiently than adding features, because surviving behavior identifies which responsibility was real.
candidatePriors.failureBoundary: Deletion is not epistemically privileged when irreversible reconstruction cost or unique evidence loss is high; archive/reversible removal is then the correct probe.

candidatePriors.name: preserve_unknowns_instead_of_forcing_completion
candidatePriors.claim: Explicit uncertainty usually preserves more future decision value than prematurely mapping unknown, stale, ambiguous, or unresolved states into success/failure labels.
candidatePriors.failureBoundary: Uncertainty retention without a reconciliation or decision policy can become passive ambiguity; tractability requires knowing when more observation is worth its cost.

candidatePriors.name: stop_when_no_causal_target_is_justified
candidatePriors.claim: A research loop should terminate or change question when additional search has no causally demonstrated target or when marginal information gain falls below its recurring cost; mutation is not evidence of progress.
candidatePriors.failureBoundary: No target under the current observation policy is not proof that no target exists; stopping must remain revisable when new evidence, capability, or cheaper observation appears.

candidatePriors.name: experimentability_can_outleverage_direct_capability
candidatePriors.claim: Improving observation, replay, recovery, exact identity, evaluation, or experiment construction can yield more compounding RSI leverage than directly adding another domain capability, because it lowers the cost of many future improvement cycles.
candidatePriors.failureBoundary: Meta-infrastructure can become self-referential overhead; it earns leverage only when ordinary workloads repeatedly consume it and total cycle cost falls.

candidatePriors.name: question_quality_is_frontier_change_not_answer_volume
candidatePriors.claim: A high-value research question is one whose possible outcomes materially change the next admissible frontier, delete a large hypothesis region, or alter future experiment cost; producing more answers without changing decisions has low marginal research value.
candidatePriors.failureBoundary: Some long-horizon basic research accumulates apparently decision-neutral observations before a frontier shift becomes visible; the heuristic should discount but not prohibit such work.

rejectedAntiPriors.claim: If a concept recurs across projects, create a shared layer.
rejectedAntiPriors.reason: Semantic convergence repeatedly survived while shared mechanism proposals were deleted, localized, or left owner-native.

rejectedAntiPriors.claim: More complete context or source coverage is always better research.
rejectedAntiPriors.reason: Harness P4 reached lawful abstention only after 203 observations and near-complete source coverage; the next open problem is explicitly smaller high-information discovery.

rejectedAntiPriors.claim: A mechanically stronger containment or binding mechanism is necessarily more semantically correct.
rejectedAntiPriors.reason: Runtime rejected sealed-memfd executable materialization as the default because it changed legitimate target-visible pathname semantics despite stronger byte isolation.

rejectedAntiPriors.claim: Every improvement cycle should end in a mutation.
rejectedAntiPriors.reason: Harness P4 falsified two Agent-selected targets and established lawful no-change semantics; World and Studio/Web also terminate phases without manufacturing changes.

rejectedAntiPriors.claim: If an experiment can generate variants cheaply, the problem is tractable.
rejectedAntiPriors.reason: Current work repeatedly shows verification, effect reconciliation, human evidence, environment setup, and observation latency dominating generation cost.

rejectedAntiPriors.claim: A broader architecture gives more leverage than a narrow local mechanism.
rejectedAntiPriors.reason: Computer, World, Runtime, Harness, and Studio/Web repeatedly retained the narrowest owner-native mechanism and rejected generic frameworks until recurrence forces promotion.

tractabilityDimensions.name: observability
tractabilityDimensions.question: Can the relevant current state and outcome be observed with enough fidelity?

tractabilityDimensions.name: discriminability
tractabilityDimensions.question: Can a bounded experiment distinguish the live competing explanations or designs?

tractabilityDimensions.name: feedback_latency
tractabilityDimensions.question: How quickly can a trustworthy outcome change the next decision?

tractabilityDimensions.name: verification_cost
tractabilityDimensions.question: What compute, human, environment, and domain work is required to tell whether the result is actually correct?

tractabilityDimensions.name: experiment_cost
tractabilityDimensions.question: What implementation, execution, data, and opportunity cost is paid before useful evidence appears?

tractabilityDimensions.name: authority_and_access
tractabilityDimensions.question: Does the Agent have an admissible observation/intervention path without silently expanding authority?

tractabilityDimensions.name: reversibility_recovery
tractabilityDimensions.question: Can failed exploration be undone, reconciled, or repeated without large irreversible loss?

tractabilityDimensions.name: branching_search_space
tractabilityDimensions.question: How many plausible branches must be explored before evidence can eliminate most of them?

tractabilityDimensions.name: generality_recurrence
tractabilityDimensions.question: Would a result recur across materially different workloads, or is it likely local?

tractabilityDimensions.name: meta_leverage
tractabilityDimensions.question: Will solving this reduce the cost or improve the fidelity of many future improvement cycles?

questionTransformationOperators.to: Which observed burden or non-bypassable responsibility would X remove, and what fails without it?

questionTransformationOperators.from: How do we solve the whole problem?
questionTransformationOperators.to: Which current bottleneck prevents the next meaningful state transition, and can one bounded experiment discriminate it?

questionTransformationOperators.from: How do we improve mechanism X?
questionTransformationOperators.to: What is the smallest falsifier that would prove X insufficient or unnecessary?
What current consumer/invariant fails if X is deleted, narrowed, localized, or replaced by the simpler baseline?

questionTransformationOperators.from: This relation appears twice; should it be shared?
questionTransformationOperators.to: Does a materially different owner reproduce the same semantic invariant and the same mechanical friction?

questionTransformationOperators.from: Can the Agent generate a better candidate?
questionTransformationOperators.to: Can the system cheaply and independently distinguish a better candidate from a plausible wrong one?

questionTransformationOperators.from: What should the loop do next?
questionTransformationOperators.to: What observation could still change the decision, what will it cost, and what condition makes abstention/termination correct?

questionTransformationOperators.from: The operation succeeded; are we done?
questionTransformationOperators.to: Which causal stage and semantic consequence were actually established, and what remains unknown?

questionTransformationOperators.from: How do we model/control the whole world?
questionTransformationOperators.to: Which owner-native boundary, relation, or consequence is currently unobservable or unactionable?
Which next observation has the highest expected discrimination or frontier-changing value relative to its cost?

currentGaps: The current Agent-First Research Method begins after a burden/question has largely been selected; it does not yet explain how an Agent ranks many candidate questions on the frontier.
The priors are not prospectively calibrated. Current evidence is retrospective and vulnerable to selection bias.
Research decisions do not consistently record rejected alternative questions and predicted information gain before outcomes are known.

Cross-project cost evidence is heterogeneous; tokens, wall time, human review, environment setup, recovery, and effect risk are not yet comparable enough for a universal score, and a universal score is not currently justified.

Harness P4 proves autonomous discovery authority but not discovery efficiency: 203 observations and near-complete source coverage leave question/observation selection as a live tractability bottleneck.
The system has no durable calibration loop that updates research-taste priors when a predicted high-value question yields little information or when a dismissed question becomes decisive.
nextFalsifier: Prospectively compare Agent frontier selection with and without a compact subset of these priors on the same real candidate-question set. Freeze candidate questions and predicted tractability dimensions before outcomes, preserve owner-native evaluation, and measure information gained, total closed-loop cost, false promotion, unnecessary exploration, and lawful abstention. Do not implement a general Tractability Engine unless repeated prospective trials show that a reusable mechanism beats a compact prompt/checklist baseline.
